headline: Beta came back — SOXX +3.9%, high-beta/low-vol +3.1% off a z=-2.0 washout — but it came back on a 97th-percentile dollar and a 2-year yield that still refuses to fall.
summary: The bid flipped from defense to beta in a single session. SPHB/SPLV jumped 3.1% and turned up from a z=-2.0 extreme; SOXX +3.9%, SMH +3.0%, AMD +5.5%, AVGO +4.0%, TSM +2.9%, MU +2.8%, ARKK +3.6%, XBI +2.9%, TSLA +4.0%. The left-for-dead cyclical wreckage ripped hardest: XME +4.7%, REMX +4.8%, URA +4.4%, NLR +4.2%, COPX +3.9%. Vol confirmed it — VIX -4.7% to 17.52, MOVE -4.2% to 97.87, back under 100 for the first time in this episode — and the rates deceleration that set this up is intact: 10y 4.99% (-18bp on the month, acc z=-1.94), 5y 4.82% (-16bp, acc -2.03), 10y real 2.64% (-19bp, acc -2.02). Risk regime improves to -15 from -19.

What changed versus yesterday is leadership, in both directions. The defensive complex that had been absorbing every dollar finally gave some back: XLP -0.9%, COST -1.3%, WMT -0.8%, USMV -0.4%, SPLV -0.2%, MCD -0.5% — even as their acceleration scores (XLU 2.33, XLP 1.89, SPLV 2.35) sit at crowded extremes. More important, energy — the only sector with rising relative strength (+10.2% 1m) — finally followed crude down. Brent -5.5% to 109.44, WTI through 100 to 99.88, and this time the equities went with it: XLE -2.1%, XOP -2.4%, XOM -2.5%, CVX -1.6%. XLE is still 18.0% above its 200-day at the 95th percentile of its year. The de-escalation that is a gift to the inflation print is a bill for the one sector carrying the index's cyclical weight. Gasoline is -9.9% on the month (z=-1.02); natural gas spiked +17.3% in a day but remains -17.2% YTD.

The tightening is now coming through FX and the front end, not the long end. DXY +0.4% to 102.36, 97th percentile of 52 weeks. EURUSD -0.8% to 1.1132 — the 0th percentile, a 52-week low, z=-1.02. USD/JPY +0.7% to 157.95, USD/CHF at the 91st percentile. Against that, the 2-year rose 2bp to 4.70% while the 10y fell 1bp and the 30y fell 1bp to 5.30%; 2s10s flattened 3bp to 29bp, 17th percentile and rolling over. The 30-year mortgage is still 7.32%, 94th percentile, and 5y breakevens are +11bp on the month at 2.45% with the inflation composite at -45. EM is where the dollar bites: USD/MXN z=1.93 at the 97th percentile (+5.3% on the month), USD/BRL 5.3513 still turning up and +6.2% on the week, KOSPI -1.5% and -22.8% on the month at z=-3.14, EEM/SPY z=-1.91 at the 16th percentile.

Breadth did not confirm the beta day, which is the caveat. SPX +0.6% and NDX +1.3% against RSP +0.1%; equal-weight/cap-weight fell 0.5% and rolled over despite the highest acceleration on the board at +3.01. IWM +1.2% and IWM/SPY +0.6% are the offset, but IWM/SPY is still at the 23rd percentile. Dispersion remains violent: BA -10.7% in a day to the 0th percentile (-24.1% over three months), META -1.6% with acceleration z=-3.03 and -17.5% on the month inside an XLC at the 0th percentile, NFLX -2.2% and -9.0% on the week, LMT giving back 1.9% after a +13.5% week. Precious metals bounced (gold +1.0% to 4,078, GDXJ +3.5%) but gold/silver is still +11.1% on the month with acceleration 1.36 — that unwind isn't finished. Growth pulse is the quiet positive: UPS +5.8% (z=1.69, acc 2.06), FDX +2.2%, DJT +1.7%, IYT/SPY acceleration +2.54, copper +2.3% with copper/gold at the 100th percentile of its year.

good.text: Bond vol broke 100: MOVE -4.2% to 97.87, with curve-wide deceleration — 2y acc z=-2.00, 5y -2.03, 10y real -2.02. The second derivative of the tightening is unambiguously negative.
Risk appetite reclaimed: high-beta/low-vol +3.1% and turning up from z=-2.0, ARKK +3.6%, XBI +2.9%, IWM +1.2%, TSLA +4.0%. Washed-out beta is being bought, not sold.
Semis led the tape for a third day and the ratio turned: SOXX +3.9%, SMH +3.0%, AMD +5.5%, AVGO +4.0%, TSM +2.9%, SMH/SPY +2.4% to turning_up off z=-1.45.
The inflation constraint keeps loosening: Brent -5.5% to 109.44, WTI back under 100 at 99.88, gasoline -9.9% on the month at z=-1.02.
Credit refuses to crack: HYG +0.5%, HYG/IEF +0.5%, BKLN at the 93rd percentile, VIX -4.7% to 17.52 and term structure back to 0.895.
Real-economy pulse firming: UPS +5.8% (acc z=2.06), FDX +2.2% (acc 1.72), DJT +1.7%, IYT/SPY acceleration +2.54, copper +2.3% with copper/gold at the 100th percentile.

bad.text: The dollar is the tightening nobody can hedge: DXY +0.4% to 102.36 at the 97th percentile, EURUSD -0.8% to 1.1132 — a 52-week low, 0th percentile — USD/CHF 91st percentile.
Front end won't play along: 2y +2bp to 4.70% on a day the 10y fell; 2s10s -3bp to 29bp at the 17th percentile and rolling over; 30-year mortgage pinned at 7.32%, 94th percentile.
Breadth did not confirm: equal-weight/cap-weight -0.5% and rolling over despite a +3.01 acceleration score; RSP +0.1% against SPX +0.6%; IWM/SPY still 23rd percentile.
Comm services is a hole in the index: META acceleration z=-3.03 and -17.5% on the month, XLC at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks, NFLX -2.2% and -9.0% on the week.
EM is absorbing the dollar: USD/MXN z=1.93 at the 97th percentile, USD/BRL still turning up and +6.2% on the week, KOSPI z=-3.14, EEM/SPY z=-1.91 at the 16th percentile.
The index's only RS-up sector started to break: XLE -2.1%, XOP -2.4%, XOM -2.5% as crude bled, from 18% above the 200-day. Cheaper oil is good for CPI and bad for 2026 earnings breadth.

trades.name: Fade extended energy equities
trades.line: Short XLE/XOP: crude premium bleeding, equities 18% over 200d
trades.expr: Short XOP outright or buy Dec/Jan XLE puts ~5% OTM; cleanest as pair — short XOP vs long SPY, dollar-neutral.
trades.thesis: Energy carried the month on a war premium that is gone. Brent at 109.44 is -5.5% in a day, WTI lost the 100 handle, gasoline is -9.9% on the month. XLE sits 18.0% above its 200-day at the 95th percentile with +10.2% one-month relative strength; XOP is 18.7% extended. Positioning is long, the catalyst is reversing, and today the equities finally stopped ignoring the barrel.
trades.trigger: XLE -2.1%, XOP -2.4%, XOM -2.5%, CVX -1.6% on a +0.6% S&P day — the first session where energy underperformed crude's decline rather than absorbing it.
trades.stop: Brent reclaims 115 or XLE makes a new high above today's level; a re-escalation headline invalidates immediately.
trades.target: XLE back toward its 200-day (-8% to -12%); XOP -15%.

trades.name: Beta over defense
trades.line: Long SPHB vs short SPLV: fade the crowded defensive bid
trades.expr: Long SPHB / short SPLV, equal dollar. Overlay: sell XLU and XLP against it if you want the sector version.
trades.thesis: The defensive trade is the most extended thing on the board — SPLV acceleration 2.35, XLU 2.33, XLP 1.89, USMV at the 96th percentile — while high-beta/low-vol washed out to z=-2.0 and turned up today. With MOVE under 100 and VIX at 17.52, the insurance premium that funded that bid is deflating.
trades.trigger: SPHB/SPLV +3.1% in one session, state flipped to turning_up; XLP -0.9%, COST -1.3%, USMV -0.4% on an up tape.
trades.stop: SPHB/SPLV closes back below 1.82 (today 1.8875) or VIX takes out 22.
trades.target: Ratio back to 2.05, roughly reversing the -12.3% one-month drawdown.

trades.name: Semis relative-strength turn
trades.line: Long SMH vs SPY: ratio turns up from z=-1.45
trades.expr: Long SMH vs short SPY, 1:1 notional; or Dec SMH 570/620 call spreads for convexity.
trades.thesis: The semis drawdown was a positioning flush, not a fundamental break — SMH is still +55% on the year with TSM, AMD and MU all in uptrends. The ratio bottomed at z=-1.45 and has now turned, three sessions into a broadening bounce that today included second-tier names (AVGO +4.0%, ASML +2.8%), not just NVDA.
trades.trigger: SOXX +3.9%, SMH/SPY +2.4% to turning_up, AMD +5.5%, MU +2.8%; QQQ/SPY also turned up (+0.7%).
trades.stop: SMH/SPY back below 0.700 (today 0.725) or SMH closes under its 200-day (7.9% below spot).
trades.target: SMH/SPY 0.785, recovering the -10.6% one-month relative loss.

trades.name: Belly duration
trades.line: Long IEF: MOVE under 100, 5y -16bp on the month, acc z=-2.03
trades.expr: Long IEF (or 5y note futures, FV). Fund partly by shorting TLT to stay off the 30-year, which is only -19bp on the month and still 5.30%.
trades.thesis: Every tenor's acceleration score is near -2.0 while bond vol just broke 100 for the first time this cycle. The belly is where a cutting Fed pays and where the inflation tail is least damaging — long-end supply and a 5.30% 30y argue against buying duration outright, so own 5-10y against the bond.
trades.trigger: MOVE -4.2% to 97.87; IEF carries the highest acceleration in the credit block at +1.69; 10y real yield -19bp on the month to 2.64%.
trades.stop: 10y back above 5.15% or 5y breakevens through 2.60% (today 2.45%, already +11bp on the month).
trades.target: 10y 4.70%, IEF +2.0-2.5%; curve flattener leg adds if 2s10s holds under 35bp.

trades.name: META as the funding short
trades.line: Short META: acceleration z=-3.03, XLC at the 0th percentile
trades.expr: Short META outright, or short META vs long QQQ to isolate the idiosyncratic leg. Options: Dec 600 puts.
trades.thesis: META has the worst acceleration reading on the entire board at -3.03, is -17.5% on the month and -10.7% on the week, and sits inside the only sector at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. It fell 1.6% on a day when high beta rose 2.9% — that is distribution, not de-risking.
trades.trigger: META -1.6% against NDX +1.3%; XLC -0.3% on an up tape and -8.3% on the month at z=-1.82; NFLX -9.0% on the week confirms the sector, not the name.
trades.stop: Close back above 680 (roughly reclaiming the 200-day, currently 1.8% above spot) or XLC relative strength turning up.
trades.target: 540, completing the -20% derating; cover half at 575.

trades.name: Transports turn
trades.expr: Long IYT, or long an equal-weight version via XTN to avoid single-name concentration; UPS and FDX are the core longs.
trades.thesis: The cyclical pulse is improving off a very low base. Transports are -9.1% relative to the S&P over three months and IYT/SPY is at the 28th percentile, but the acceleration is the highest in the factor block at +2.54, and the two bellwethers are both making their best moves of the year.
trades.trigger: UPS +5.8% (z=1.69, acc 2.06), FDX +2.2% (acc 1.72), DJT +1.7% to turning_up, XTN +2.5%, all with crude falling — the fuel input is deflating into a demand upturn.
trades.stop: IYT/SPY back below 0.1040 or DJT losing its 200-day (0.7% below spot).
trades.target: IYT +8-10%; ratio back to the 50th percentile of its year.

trades.name: Short the peso into a 97th-percentile dollar
trades.line: Long USDMXN: peso z=1.93 while MXX runs +7.3% on the month
trades.expr: Long USD/MXN spot or 3-month forward; equity-market version is short EWW (peso-exposed) vs long MXX-equivalent local exposure.
trades.thesis: Mexican equities are celebrating (MXX +7.3% on the month, z=1.53, 81st percentile) while the currency is quietly breaking — USD/MXN +5.3% on the month at the 97th percentile with z=1.93 and 6.9% above its 200-day. That divergence resolves through the currency when DXY is making 52-week highs and EM FX broadly (CEW -1.0% on the week) is rolling.
trades.trigger: DXY +0.4% to 102.36 at the 97th percentile; EURUSD at the 0th percentile; EWW -0.4% today against MXX +0.3% — the FX leak is already showing in the dollar-denominated ETF.
trades.stop: USD/MXN back below 17.90 or DXY losing 101.00.
